title: Updating and checking changes
goal: Verify configuration and database changes on a copy while preserving recovery.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 3; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: Verify configuration and database changes on a copy while preserving recovery.
Compare editable and database configuration before applying.
Apply only the agreed diff to the copy.
sections: The editable configuration and database configuration can differ before applying a change. Saving development text does not necessarily update the running database structure. Record both versions and expected state. When updating a copy, inspect restructuring warnings and do not approve deletion of objects outside the agreed diff.

Begin by asking whether an existing setting solves the request. A personal list variant needs no storage change; an absent required attribute needs a model and rules. Record the chosen mechanism and rejected alternative. This lets maintainers understand the decision without repeating experiments and avoids unnecessary implementation scope.

A successful configuration check detects some metadata and module errors but does not prove a business workflow. Open an old request, create a new one, apply a filter and reconcile totals. For a new attribute, check input, save and reread. Valid metadata with a rejected document can still indicate a behavior problem.

Field types determine operations and boundaries. A string identifier preserves leading zeros, a number supports arithmetic, and a reference supports identity. Specify ordinary, empty and maximum-value examples before applying. Define old-record behavior separately:new fields must not silently rewrite the meaning of an accepted request. Check both existing and newly created documents.

Restoring an old field name does not recover deleted values. A rollback path relies on a preserved copy of data and configuration, verified by restoration into a new directory. Do not load an old configuration over the only updated infobase. Preserve the source and a separate updated instance with explicit provenance.

Applying a change differs from saving development text. Compare editable and database configurations, review the intended diff and restructuring warnings. Update a separate copy and repeat user workflows. A technically valid schema can behave incorrectly, so combine configuration checking with input, writing, reports and fresh reads of old data. One layer does not establish the others.
A change record links expectation and observation

Record purpose, versions, diff, test inputs, outcomes and the safe copy reference. Preserve a failed experiment separately rather than hiding it behind a successful retry. Exclude passwords, real data and private paths from published evidence. When a warning is unclear, stop that application step while continuing independent checks on the preserved source.

Rollback preserves data state as well as code. Renaming a removed field back cannot recover lost values. Verify backup by restoring to a fresh directory and reconciling control records. Keep source and upgraded work as separate instances. If a warning exceeds agreed scope, do not approve blindly; preserve it and investigate on the copy.

lab.title: Verify configuration and database changes on a copy while preserving recovery.
lab.environment: Official 1C 8.3.27.x, new training-service-desk copy. Command labels depend on the configuration interface; verify outcomes against data. Training-edition limits are explicit.
steps: Create a separate work copy; record its ID, source ID and platform/configuration build. Never restore over your source.
Compare editable and database configuration before applying.
Apply only the agreed diff to the copy.
Restore the prior backup into a third fresh directory.
Reopen the copy, repeat the checks and reconcile the unchanged source. Preserve failures separately from the corrected attempt.
expected: The version difference is recorded; data is not assumed updated.
Old records remain readable; the new field persists.
Version v1 and control data are restored without overwriting v2.
evidence: Input/expected/actual/case-ID table, platform build and source hashes.
The source remains v1; copy v2 stores the new field and old records.
Work-copy provenance, negative result and source preservation before/after.
lab.negative: Version v1 and control data are restored without overwriting v2.

mistakes: Treat an expected value as an observed execution.
Reconcile the result in the specified environment and attach the protocol; the browser model does not execute BSL.
Modify the source infobase while experimenting.
Work on a new copy and verify the source by reopening it separately.

quiz.question: Does saving development always update database structure?
What recovers lost data?
quiz.explanation: Names do not contain deleted values.

quiz.question: Is syntax PASS sufficient to accept a change?
options: No; workflows and data need checks
quiz.explanation: Valid syntax does not prove behavior.
